task: Necroptosis cert (3rd panel of the cell-death triad, completing apoptosis [scripts/msk/apoptosis_intrinsic_extrinsic.py] + ferroptosis [docs/MECHANISM_FERROPTOSIS.md]): the RIPK1->RIPK3->MLKL necrosome axis, unmasked by caspase-8 inhibition (canonical TNF+SMAC-mimetic+zVAD trigger); RIPK3-mediated MLKL phosphorylation -> oligomerization -> plasma-membrane pore -> lytic death; the defining CASPASE-8/RIPK relationship (caspase-8 normally cleaves RIPK1 to suppress necroptosis -- caspase inhibition PROMOTES it, opposite of apoptosis).

degterev_2005_necroptosis_discovery.numbers: FOUNDING paper. Coins the term 'necroptosis': Fas/TNFR engagement, in the absence of intracellular apoptotic signaling, activates 'a common nonapoptotic death pathway.' In-vivo anchor: necroptosis contributes to delayed mouse ischemic brain injury via a mechanism distinct from apoptosis.

he_2009_rip3_determinant.cite: He S, Wang L, Miao L, Wang T, Du F, Zhao L, Wang X (2009). "Receptor interacting protein kinase-3 determines cellular necrotic response to TNF-alpha." Cell 137(6):1100-11.
he_2009_rip3_determinant.verified_via: NCBI esearch (title match) + esummary + efetch abstract, live this session. Author-affiliation cross-check via Europe PMC authorList API: last/senior author confirmed as Xiaodong Wang (ORCID-linked full name), first author He S affiliated 'Graduate Program, Peking Union Medical College and Chinese Academy of Medical Sciences, Beijing, China.' NO PMC full text available this session (paywalled, disclosed).
he_2009_rip3_determinant.numbers: Exact quote: 'Smac mimetics induce apoptosis synergistically with TNF-alpha by triggering the formation of a caspase-8-activating complex containing receptor interacting protein kinase-1 (RIPK1). Caspase inhibitors block this form of apoptosis in many types of cells. However, in several other cell lines, caspase inhibitors switch the apoptotic response to necrosis.' -- THE canonical TNF+Smac-mimetic+pan-caspase-inhibitor trigger logic. Genome-wide siRNA screen identifies RIP3 as required for necrosis; kinase activity of RIP3 essential for execution; RIP3 recruited to RIPK1 to form a necrosis-inducing complex. RIP3-KO MEFs resistant to necrosis; RIP3-KO mice 'devoid of inflammation inflicted tissue damage in an acute pancreatitis model' (2nd, in-vivo, non-cell-death-assay system).

cho_2009_rip1rip3_necrosome.cite: Cho YS, Challa S, Moquin D, Genga R, Ray TD, Guildford M, Chan FK (2009). "Phosphorylation-driven assembly of the RIP1-RIP3 complex regulates programmed necrosis and virus-induced inflammation." Cell 137(6):1112-23.
cho_2009_rip1rip3_necrosome.verified_via: NCBI esearch (title match) + esummary + OWN PMC full-text XML fetch, live this session. cho_2009_rip1rip3_necrosome.numbers: Own extraction from Results text: RIP3-specific siRNAs 'inhibited TNF/zVAD-fmk-induced programmed necrosis... but had little or no effect on apoptosis induced by TNF or FasL' -- necroptosis-specific, apoptosis-neutral. Kinase-dead RIP3 (D161N) and a RIP1 RHIM-domain mutant each block programmed necrosis (kinase/scaffold activity itself required, not mere complex formation). 'The RIP1 kinase inhibitor necrostatin-1 (Nec-1) potently inhibited Complex II kinase activity.' RIP3 constitutively associated with FADD; RIP1 recruited to Complex II ('the necrosome') severely impaired in RIP3-/- MEFs; Nec-1 abolished RIP1 recruitment to FADD.

zhang_2009_rip3_switch.cite: Zhang DW, Shao J, Lin J, Zhang N, Lu BJ, Lin SC, Dong MQ, Han J (2009). "RIP3, an energy metabolism regulator that switches TNF-induced cell death from apoptosis to necrosis." Science 325(5938):332-6.

zhang_2009_rip3_switch.numbers: Exact quote: 'RIP3 did not affect RIP1-mediated apoptosis but was required for RIP1-mediated necrosis and the enhancement of necrosis by the caspase inhibitor zVAD.' -- the precise, genetically-anchored statement that zVAD's necrosis-PROMOTING effect is itself RIP3-dependent, not a generic off-target toxicity. RIP3 activates key metabolic enzymes, regulates TNF-induced ROS production, partially accounting for its necrosis-promoting role.

murphy_2013_mlkl_structure_switch.numbers: Own MLKL-deficient mice generated: 'viable and displayed no hematopoietic anomalies or other obvious pathology' but cells 'resistant to TNF-induced necroptosis unless MLKL expression was restored' -- necroptosis-specific, not a general developmental lesion. Crystal structure: 4-helix bundle tethered to a catalytically-inactive pseudokinase domain that binds ATP; RIPK3-mediated phosphorylation of the pseudoactive site is the essential nonenzymatic trigger. Structure-guided pseudoactive-site mutation causes constitutive, RIPK3-INDEPENDENT necroptosis -- a gain-of-function proof that this specific modification, not RIPK3 itself, is the terminal switch.

lin_1999_caspase8_cleaves_rip1.cite: Lin Y, Devin A, Rodriguez Y, Liu ZG (1999). "Cleavage of the death domain kinase RIP by caspase-8 prompts TNF-induced apoptosis." Genes Dev 13(19):2514-26.
lin_1999_caspase8_cleaves_rip1.verified_via: NCBI esearch (title match) + esummary + efetch abstract, live this session.
lin_1999_caspase8_cleaves_rip1.numbers: THE founding molecular relationship, 6 years before 'necroptosis' was named and 10 years before RIPK3/MLKL were identified. Exact quote: 'the death domain kinase RIP... was cleaved by Caspase-8 in TNF-induced apoptosis. The cleavage site was mapped to the aspartic acid at position 324 of RIP... cleavage of RIP resulted in the blockage of TNF-induced NF-kappaB activation... the Caspase-8 resistant RIP mutants protected cells against TNF-induced apoptosis[-pathway consequences].' Establishes that caspase-8 acts DIRECTLY and SPECIFICALLY on RIP1 (RIPK1) at a mapped cleavage site, not merely 'in a parallel pathway' -- the molecular basis for why caspase-8 loss/inhibition specifically unmasks RIPK1-dependent signaling.

kaiser_2011_rip3_rescues_casp8ko.cite: Kaiser WJ, Upton JW, Long AB, Livingston-Rosanoff D, Daley-Bauer LP, Hakem R, Caspary T, Mocarski ES (2011). "RIP3 mediates the embryonic lethality of caspase-8-deficient mice." Nature 471(7338):368-72.
kaiser_2011_rip3_rescues_casp8ko.verified_via: NCBI esearch (title match) + esummary + OWN PMC full-text XML fetch, live this session. Corresponding author confirmed via own full-text extraction: William J. Kaiser, Emory Vaccine Center, Emory University School of Medicine.
kaiser_2011_rip3_rescues_casp8ko.numbers: Exact quotes: 'Disruption of Casp8 expression leads to embryonic lethality in mice between embryonic days 10.5 and 11.5... We find that RIP3 is responsible for the mid-gestational death of Casp8-deficient embryos... Casp8-/-Rip3-/- double mutant mice are viable and mature into fertile adults with a full immune complement of myeloid and lymphoid cell types... RIP3 and Casp8 are together completely dispensable for mammalian development.' Own full-text extraction: within the SAME intercross/litter, Casp8-/-Rip3+/- embryos (RIP3 still present) arrest at ~E11.0 -- isolating RIP3 dosage as the specific rescuing variable, not a generic strain-background effect. DKO adults later develop lymphadenopathy (~4 months), resist anti-Fas (Jo-2) lethal challenge, resembling lpr/lpr (Fas-deficient) mice.

The 'without inducing apoptosis' clause is the critical mechanistic disambiguator -- rules out 'the rescue just restores a missed apoptotic program' as the explanation.

Reciprocal, partial rescue also shown: FADD deletion partially corrects RIP1-/- lymphocyte proliferation defects (T cells fully, B cells not) -- a cell-type-specific asymmetry, honestly reported by the source paper itself, not smoothed over.
